allow_large: Owner-approved 2026-09-29 for legacy clean-ups: removes field-specific rejections for job fields that no longer exist; those fields now get the generic unknown-field rejection; no new API surface
done_when: The jobs API, IPC task parsing and scheduler MCP tools no longer mention groupScope, group_scope, requiredTools, required_tools or GANTRY_GROUP_FOLDER; the tool schema no longer advertises required_tools; tests updated

dismissals.because: apps/core/test/unit/control/specific-no-longer-accepted-errors-for-r.test.ts:35 owner's standing rule (2026-09-29): no tests may name removed fields, and end-to-end tests proving a pure deletion stays deleted are dismissed; current behaviour (unknown fields rejected) is covered with neutral names

findings.body: The HTTP test sends `unexpectedField`, which already received the same generic response before this fix; restoring the deleted field-specific errors would leave it passing. The IPC test calls the parser directly, and the scheduler tests capture schemas/handlers rather than exercising the MCP entry point. No remaining behavioral test verifies that discovery omits `required_tools` or that startup succeeds with `GANTRY_GROUP_FOLDER` present. This fails the explicit end-to-end regression-test requirement. Add suite-wired tests through the real API, IPC and MCP entry points that exercise the removed names, verify generic handling and advertised schemas, and cover startup with the obsolete environment variable. These tests must fail when the corresponding old behavior returns.
findings.title: Not done: End-to-end regression tests for removed job and scheduler fields

why: Specific 'no longer accepted' errors for removed job and scheduler fields keep old field names alive, and required_tools is still shown to the model as a deprecated tool parameter
